descriptionChirho: The place or act of meeting, predominantly in the phrase ohel moed (tent of meeting); Arabic الاِجْتِمَاعِ (al-ijtimāʿ, gathering), Korean 만남 (mannam, meeting), Swahili mkutano (meeting), Hindi मिलाप (milāp, meeting), Spanish reunión all consistently point to 'meeting/assembly' as a distinct sense from 'appointed time' or 'feast'

A designated or fixed point in time; Arabic مِيعَاد/مَوْعِد (mīʿād/mawʿid, appointment), Korean 정한 때 (jeonghan ttae, appointed time), Swahili wakati (time), Hindi नियत समय (niyat samay, fixed time), Spanish tiempo señalado all converge on temporal appointment rather than festival or place

Religious festivals and appointed seasons of worship; Arabic مَوْسِم (mawsim, season/festival) and أَعْيَاد (aʿyād, festivals), Korean 절기 (jeolgi, festival season), Swahili sikukuu (holiday/festival), Hindi पर्व (parv, festival), Spanish fiesta/fiestas señaladas all distinguish this from mere temporal appointment — these are the cyclical sacred observances of Israel

A designated location for assembly or encounter, distinct from the tent-of-meeting formula; Arabic مَحْفَل (maḥfal, assembly hall) and مَحافِل (maḥāfil, assembly places), Korean 모임 터 (moim teo, gathering place), Swahili mahali pa mkutano (place of meeting), Spanish lugar de reunión — the spatial rather than temporal or cultic sense

A pre-arranged sign or signal for coordinated action; Arabic مَوْعِد here in the sense of a signal agreed upon beforehand, Korean 신호 (sinho, signal), Swahili ishara (signal/sign), Hindi निशानी (nishānī, sign/mark), Spanish señal (signal) — a rare but distinct sense attested in Judges 20:38
